titleEn: Social media provides valued community spaces for autistic young people
titleZh: 社交媒体为自闭症青少年提供珍贵的社群空间
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition which influences how people communicate and process information. A significant proportion of autistic children do not speak, or only speak a few words. Many find it difficult to communicate face to face, especially when interaction is fast moving or dependent on interpreting bodily cues.
paragraphs.zh: 自闭症是一种影响人们交流和处理信息的神经发育状况。有相当一部分自闭症儿童不说话，或只说几句话。许多人发现面对面交流很困难，特别是当互动是快速移动的或依赖于解释身体暗示时。

paragraphs.en: Social media offers what can be an easier way for autistic people to socially interact. When communication takes place over text, there is no need to make eye contact or interpret facial expressions. There is also more time to read a message, consider a reply and participate without the sensory demands of a busy room. Although online interactions are not free of misunderstanding, for some autistic young people they provide a form of social contact that is more manageable than many physical settings.
paragraphs.zh: 社交媒体为自闭症患者提供了一种更简单的社交方式。当交流通过文本进行时，不需要进行眼神交流或解读面部表情。也有更多的时间来阅读信息、考虑回复和参与，而不需要在忙碌的房间里进行感官需求。尽管在线互动并非没有误解，对于一些患有自闭症的年轻人来说，他们提供了一种比许多物理环境更容易管理的社会接触形式。

paragraphs.en: Many autistic people have at least one area of highly intense interest. These interests can often be quite niche and so there may not be any local clubs or groups.
paragraphs.zh: 许多自闭症患者至少有一个领域有着强烈的兴趣。这些兴趣往往是相当小众的，所以可能没有任何当地的俱乐部或团体。

paragraphs.en: As part of the Autism in Affinity Spaces project, based at Queen Mary University of London, we are investigating how and why young autistic people in the UK use social media to engage with their focused interests during the transition to adulthood. We have conducted a survey with 144 young people aged between 16 and 26 to find out more about their experiences.
paragraphs.zh: 作为伦敦玛丽女王大学“亲密空间中的自闭症”项目的一部分，我们正在调查英国年轻自闭症患者在成年过渡期如何以及为什么使用社交媒体来参与他们关注的兴趣。我们对144名年龄在16至26岁之间的年轻人进行了调查，以了解他们的更多经历。

paragraphs.en: The benefits of social media
paragraphs.zh: 社交媒体的优势

paragraphs.en: Since social media offers connections across the globe, our participants told us that they used spaces such as Facebook groups and Discord servers to connect with people who shared their interests and understood why they mattered. One participant explained:
paragraphs.zh: 由于社交媒体在地球仪内提供了联系，我们的参与者告诉我们，他们使用Facebook群组和Discord服务器等空间与那些与他们有共同兴趣并理解他们为什么重要的人建立联系。一名参与者解释说：

paragraphs.en: It’s really all about that sense of community that I didn’t have before. It’s just been so, so nice to find people that who can like an artist as much as you and understand it on the same wavelength. That’s something I haven’t had for so long.
paragraphs.zh: 这一切都是关于我以前没有的那种社区意识。找到像你一样喜欢一个艺术家并且能以同样的方式理解它的人真是太好了。这是我很久没有过的。

paragraphs.en: This was also true for non-speaking participants. One Reddit user described the value of being able to choose smaller groups and write in detail:
paragraphs.zh: 对于不说话的参与者来说也是如此。一位Reddit用户描述了能够选择更小的小组并详细书写的价值：

paragraphs.en: Since I’ve used it for years it’s easy to use. I also enjoy the anonymity. I often need long posts to explain things, and it’s quite easy to find posts about specific topics.
paragraphs.zh: 因为我已经用了很多年了，所以它很容易使用。我也很喜欢匿名。我经常需要很长的帖子来解释事情，而且很容易找到关于特定主题的帖子。

paragraphs.en: Social media also provides opportunities for learning. All our participants said they used digital platforms to learn more about their interests – for example, by watching informative YouTube videos or following experts on Instagram. Many had also become experts themselves as a result and used social media to share their knowledge with others.
paragraphs.zh: 社交媒体也提供了学习的机会。我们的所有参与者都表示，他们通过数字平台来了解更多自己的兴趣爱好--例如，观看内容丰富的YouTube视频，或在Instagram上关注专家。许多人因此也成为了专家，并通过社交媒体与他人分享自己的知识。

paragraphs.en: Importantly, social media did not displace offline activities but enhanced our participants’ ability to participate in them. Predictability and structure are often important for autistic people, so some participants used social media to research unfamiliar places or upcoming events before they went in.
paragraphs.zh: 重要的是，社交媒体并没有取代线下活动，而是增强了参与者参与其中的能力。可预测性和结构性对自闭症患者来说往往很重要，因此一些参与者在进入之前会使用社交媒体研究不熟悉的地方或即将发生的事件。

paragraphs.en: What are the downsides?
paragraphs.zh: 缺点是什么？？

paragraphs.en: Our participants also described some of the problems associated with social media, including misinformation and exposure to harmful content, such as videos promoting disordered eating after viewing content about veganism. These concerns closely reflect those raised in the government’s proposals.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的参与者还描述了一些与社交媒体相关的问题，包括错误信息和接触有害内容，例如在观看有关素食主义的内容后宣传饮食失调的视频。这些问题与政府提案中提出的问题密切相关。

paragraphs.en: However, participants on the upper age range of our sample (24-26) reported the same issues with those on the lower age range, suggesting that these harms are linked less to young people’s use of platforms than to how they are designed.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，在我们的样本中，年龄段较高的参与者（24-26岁）报告了与年龄段较低的参与者相同的问题，这表明这些伤害与年轻人使用平台的关系较小，而与平台的设计方式关系较大。

paragraphs.en: The transition to adulthood is difficult for all young people, but autistic people face unique challenges and often experience mental health difficulties as a result. As part of the updated national strategy for autistic people in England, the government has committed to supporting positive transitions and improving mental health outcomes.
paragraphs.zh: 对于所有的年轻人来说，向成年的过渡都是困难的，但自闭症患者面临着独特的挑战，并经常因此而经历心理健康方面的困难。作为英国更新的自闭症患者国家战略的一部分，政府承诺支持积极的过渡和改善心理健康结果。

paragraphs.en: While our research focused on young people aged 16 and over, a ban on social media could make these issues worse in practice for younger children, while proposed measures for the UK such as a social media curfew for under-18s could affect older teens negatively. Removing access to social media would mean the loss of those online communities which provide an important source of learning and social interaction, potentially making autistic adolescents feel even more socially isolated.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然我们的研究主要针对16岁及以上的年轻人，但禁止社交媒体可能会使这些问题在实践中对年龄较小的孩子变得更糟，而在英国提出的措施（如对18岁以下的青少年实行社交媒体宵禁）可能会对年龄较大的青少年产生负面影响。取消社交媒体的访问将意味着失去那些提供重要学习和社交来源的在线社区。潜在地使自闭症青少年感到更加的社会孤立。

paragraphs.en: Although many of our participants wanted to attend more in-person activities, they were’t always able to do so. Restricting social media will not make public transport easier to use, youth clubs more welcoming or local venues less overwhelming. It will remove a route through which young people currently gather the information and contacts needed to navigate those settings.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管我们的许多参与者希望参加更多的面对面活动，但他们并不总是能够这样做。限制社交媒体不会使公共交通更容易使用，青年俱乐部更受欢迎，当地场馆也不会那么拥挤。它将消除年轻人目前收集信息和联系所需的途径。

paragraphs.en: Changing the online environment
paragraphs.zh: 改变在线环境

paragraphs.en: If social media platforms create risks for young people, the first responsibility should lie with the companies that design them. Platforms should be expected to respond effectively to harassment and discrimination. Small design changes could also make platforms easier to manage. Young people in our current project, for example, wanted to be able to turn off scrolling or hide video recommendations – simple features that would give users more control over their own experience.
paragraphs.zh: 如果社交媒体平台给年轻人带来了风险，那么设计这些平台的公司应该承担首要责任。平台应该对骚扰和歧视做出有效回应。小小的设计变化也可以让平台更容易管理。例如，我们当前项目中的年轻人，希望能够关闭滚动或隐藏视频推荐-简单的功能，让用户更多地控制自己的体验。

paragraphs.en: Young people also need support to navigate digital spaces, including understanding how algorithms shape what they see, how to recognise misinformation and what to do when content or interaction becomes overwhelming.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人还需要支持来浏览数字空间，包括了解算法如何塑造他们所看到的，如何识别错误信息以及当内容或互动变得势不可挡时该怎么办。

paragraphs.en: But safer online spaces cannot be considered separately from the offline world. Many autistic young people use online communities because local groups do not always accommodate different communication and sensory needs. If policy aims to encourage more in-person activity, those environments must also be designed so neurodivergent people can participate.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，更安全的网络空间不能与线下世界分开考虑。许多自闭症年轻人使用网络社区，因为当地群体并不总是能满足不同的沟通和感官需求。如果政策旨在鼓励更多的面对面活动，这些环境也必须设计成让神经分歧者能够参与。
